<thought>Based on the 13C NMR chemical shifts, the molecule contains one carbon bearing three oxygens (≈ 89 ppm), three carbons each attached to a single oxygen (≈ 68–70 ppm), and the remaining aliphatic carbons (≈ 14–31 ppm). These correspond to three distinct connected fragments that can be joined to reconstruct the whole C₆H₁₄O₃ structure:
1. A carbon attached to three hydroxyl groups – SMILES C(O)(O)O  
2. A carbon attached to a single hydroxyl group – SMILES CO  
3. A plain aliphatic carbon – SMILES C  

Thus the list of SMILES strings for the connected fragments is: ['C(O)(O)O', 'CO', 'C'].</thought>
<final_answer>['C(O)(O)O', 'CO', 'C']</final_answer>
